newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 4.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul.
Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Government finalises labor law revision bill allowing corporations to lay off workers as part of downsizing and other inevitable circumstance, and to recruit substitute workers to replace workers on strike: the bill paves way for organizing plural trade unions in a single workplace: trade union dismisses the bill as worse reform, vows to stage general strike around Dec. 13: employers are opposed to the plural trade unions.
- President Kim to visit Japan January 25-26 for summit talks.
- Government to spend one trillion won over four years until 2000 to launch projects aimed at ensuring stable livelihood of workers.
- A three-member chinese military delegation scheduled to visit South Korea December 7-14 for the first time since establishment of diplomatic relations in 1992: Korea embassy in beijing.
- Multiple trade unions allowed: workers to be able to engage in political ativities.
- Ukrainian president due here December 15 for four-day visit.
- Final government draft labor law revision bill allows teachers union in 1999, recognises plural labor unions at worksite.
- Kim to visit Japan January 25 for summit with Hashimoto.
